key_insight: Torque-ripple-induced rotor oscillations feed back into the magnetic field, creating additional Maxwell pressure harmonics missed by conventional uncoupled models.
engineering_relevance: Capturing these additional pressure waves can improve NVH predictions because they may excite stator structural modes.
method: Derive nonlinear rigid-rotor dynamics under a single torque harmonic.
Extend the analysis to a flexible rotor with torsional modes using FEM.
Couple rotor dynamics and subdomain electromagnetics to evaluate air-gap field modulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports model-based findings of new rotor-motion harmonics, a slight mean-speed reduction, and additional spatio-temporal Maxwell pressure harmonics, without quantitative metrics or experimental validation details.
watch_item: Experimental validation and the computational cost of strong magneto-mechanical coupling are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Impact of Torque Ripple Induced Angular Oscillations on Maxwell Pressure Harmonics in Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Machines
